svg.aria-label: arcp interaction flows: sidecar mode sequence where the host owns the loop, harness mode sequence where arcp owns the loop, a scheduling-boundary ownership table, and a runtime integration matrix.
svg.text: interactive — the HOST owns the loop; arcp observes, fixes leaks, advises
agent loop — cadence, context, and tool use are the host's decisions

text.tspan: advisory (dotted): non-convergence warning · cache-geometry alert · spend

svg.text: surfaced in the host UI via the L1 plugin — never auto-acted
10 task-total bill · trace archived · diagnosis summary
Boundary: host schedules calls and owns context; arcp owns accounting, Class-S hygiene, advice — and exactly the actuators the host granted.
batch — ARCP owns the loop; hosts are headless executors · calibrate / experiment / CI
for each cell — arcp schedules everything outside the agent's own reasoning

text.tspan: launch with config applied (A1 · A2 · steering · context strategy)

svg.text: 4 agent loop runs; every call taps trace + cost

text.tspan: A3 rerun / A4 stop — policy-scheduled, no host permission needed

svg.text: 9 frontier report → user locks ONE static config
Boundary: arcp schedules cells, configs, reruns, stops, grading; the agent still owns its inner reasoning; backend just serves.
the locked config feeds SIDECAR via config.apply — harness decides, sidecar lives it
WHO DECIDES WHAT — the scheduling boundary
the same decision can change owner across modes; that is the point
When to call the model / loop cadence
What is in the context (composition, compaction)
Per-call knobs — A2 effort · Class S hygiene
HOST config; arcp per task if granted
Reading: HOST = the runtime's orchestrator · ARCP = policy from calibrate evidence · NEGOTIATED = capability handshake over the control protocol.
Arrows: solid = LLM traffic · dashed = control directives · dotted = advisory
Ring 0: zero cooperation · Ring 1: what the plugin API grants · Ring 2: a headless run command.
The two modes close one loop: HARNESS produces the evidence (frontier + A/A floor) → the user locks a static config → SIDECAR applies it via config.apply and meters real usage →
drift in the meter triggers the next calibrate. Advisory never auto-acts; directives never exceed granted capabilities; content is never rewritten in either mode.
Draft for maintainer review — companion to arcp Architecture v0.3 (hourglass diagram). Ring-availability cells for non-openCode hosts are design intent, to be verified per host.
